title: Finite forward product on a pair of compactifications
statement:
Use the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, the ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories on small pro-etale sites, and their pullback, tensor and signed symmetry [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $f:X\to B$ and $g:Z\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $P=X\times_B Z$, with projections $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Z$, and $h=fp=gq$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ have etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Use the chosen-compactification maps $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ and $\operatorname{PF}$ of [def-exchange-projection], and the normalized comparisons $\alpha$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Require that every tensor object in the following forward composite be bounded below and of etale origin. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{f,g}(M,N)={}&\alpha_{g,q}\circ Rg_!\bigl(\operatorname{PF}_{q,Lp^*M,N}\bigr)
\circ Rg_!\bigl(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}\otimes1_N\bigr)\\
&\circ Rg_!(\sigma_{N,Lg^*Rf_!M})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,Rf_!M}\circ\sigma_{Rf_!M,Rg_!N}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This is a map $Rf_!M\otimes_A^LRg_!N\to Rh_!(Lp^*M\otimes_A^LLq^*N)$.
Choose compactifications $f=aj$ and $g=bk$, with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Z\hookrightarrow\bar Z$ open, $a:\bar X\to B$, $b:\bar Z\to B$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $C=\bar X\times_B\bar Z$, with projections $r:C\to\bar X$, $t:C\to\bar Z$, structure map $c=ar=bt$, and open $u=j\times_B k:P\hookrightarrow C$. Write $H=j_!M$, $J=k_!N$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and $D=Lp^*M\otimes_A^LLq^*N$. Let
$$e:Lr^*H\otimes_A^LLt^*J\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!D$$
be the composite of open base change and the open tensor isomorphisms [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], first extending from $P$ to $X\times_B\bar Z$ and then to $C$, normalized to restrict to $1_D$ on $P$.
Define the entirely ordinary direct-image map
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_{a,b}(H,J)={}&\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}\circ Rb_*\bigl(\pi_{t,Lr^*H,J}\bigr)
\circ Rb_*\bigl(\operatorname{Ex}_{*,a,b,H}\otimes1_J\bigr)\\
&\circ Rb_*(\sigma_{J,Lb^*Ra_*H})\circ\pi_{b,J,Ra_*H}\circ\sigma_{Ra_*H,Rb_*J},
\end{aligned}
$$
where $\pi$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ are the counit-defined maps of [def-exchange-projection], and $\kappa_{b,t}:Rc_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rb_*Rt_*$ is the canonical direct-image compositor [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. Its target is $Rc_*(Lr^*H\otimes_A^LLt^*J)$. Under the normalized compactification identifications $Rf_!M\cong Ra_*H$, $Rg_!N\cong Rb_*J$ and $Rh_!D\cong Rc_*u_!D$ [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], the specified morphisms satisfy
$$T_{f,g}(M,N)=Rc_*(e)\circ\Omega_{a,b}(H,J).$$
This equality holds for any choices of the original compactifications defining the forward maps and for any displayed pair $(aj,bk)$, using the normalized comparisons to identify their source and target. It requires no constructibility or finite Tor amplitude and no inverse to a projection or exchange transformation. No exceptional adjoint or abstract six-functor datum is supplied.

source.place: Symmetry paragraph, reduction to proper maps by compactification: agent-formulated finite-level comparison without the finite-Tor or abstract-datum hypotheses of that paragraph.

proof.text: Work throughout at $A=A_{E,n}$ with ordinary derived tensor; write $P_v=Lv^*$ and $R_v=Rv_*$, and suppress only the canonical pullback/tensor/direct-image compositors. Use $\epsilon_o:o_!P_o\to1$ for an open-adjunction counit, to distinguish it from the proper-adjunction counits defining $\pi$. All calculations below take place in the ambient unbounded categories. Compactification and composition isomorphisms are used only on bounded-below etale-origin objects, as required in the item. The definitions give the chosen-candidate formulas for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ and $\operatorname{PF}$; the composition theorem gives the witnessed-domain $\alpha$. We prove the equality first for the displayed $(j,a)$ and $(k,b)$.

source.place: Opening paragraph: specified operations; worker expansion of the proper-reduction calculation

proof.text: Set $W=\overline X\times_B Z$, with $v:W\to Z$, $i:W\hookrightarrow C$ and $j_q:P\hookrightarrow W$. Thus $q=vj_q$, $ti=kv$ and $ij_q=u$. The square $(i,v,k,t)$ is Cartesian. Both $v$ and $t$ are base changes of $a$, hence proper; $i$ and $j_q$ are base changes of the opens $k$ and $j$. All these schemes are finite type over $k$: proper maps are finite type, and finite type is stable under composition and base change. They are Noetherian since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$) and finite type over a Noetherian scheme preserves that property. Opens in a Noetherian scheme are Noetherian and quasi-compact, so $k$ and $i$ are quasi-compact open immersions as required below. Thus $(j_q,v)$ compactifies $q$, and $(u,c)$ compactifies $h$ since $c=bt$ is proper. These are compatible compactifications in the triangle of [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate]. Write $\Gamma:k_!R_v\to R_ti_!$ for its normalized proper/open mate. The composition comparison in these coordinates is $\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b\Gamma$, with the open compositor $i_!j_{q!}\cong u_!$ inserted. This uses the description of $\alpha$ as the normalized triangle mate, not an inversion of $\Gamma$ on arbitrary inputs.

source.place: Proper reduction: compatible product compactifications and the composition triangle

proof.text:
Put $L=R_aH$, $L_0=P_bL$, $F=P_rH$, $E=P_iF$, $K=j_{q!}P_pM$, and $K_D=j_{q!}D$. The open base-change isomorphism is $\beta:E\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Write
$$A=\operatorname{Ex}_{*,a,b,H}:L_0\to R_tF,\qquad \rho_F:P_kR_tF\xrightarrow{\sim}R_vP_iF.$$
Here $\rho$ is open restriction from [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction]. It is also $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,t,k}$: on a K-injective representative its restriction formula has transpose $P_i(\varepsilon_t)$ under $P_v\dashv R_v$, exactly the transpose in [def-exchange-projection]. Horizontal mate pasting along $g=bk$ therefore gives
$$B_0:=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}=R_v(\beta)\,\rho_F\,P_k(A):P_kL_0\to R_vK.$$
The last factor $R_v(\beta)$ is the open factor for the compactification $(j,a)$ of $f$. There is no exchange for $q$ in this formula.

source.place: Proper-reduction mate calculation: exchange pasting along the actual base-change map $g=bk$

proof.text:
Let $m=i_!K$, $\chi=\epsilon_{i,F}\,i_!(\beta^{-1}):m\to F$, and $s=\Gamma_K\,k_!(B_0):k_!P_kL_0\to R_tm$. The needed square has vertical maps $\epsilon_{k,L_0}$ and $R_t\chi$, and its equation is
$$R_t(\chi)\,s=A\,\epsilon_{k,L_0}.\tag{*}$$
Here is the counit check. The normalized $\Gamma_E$ is the $k_!\dashv P_k$ adjunct of $\lambda_E^{-1}$, where $\lambda_E=P_kR_ti_!E\xrightarrow{\rho}R_vP_ii_!E\cong R_vE$ [lem-sf-proper-open-tensor-compatibility]. Naturality of $\rho$ and $P_i(\epsilon_{i,F})$ times the open unit equal to $1_E$ give
$$\rho_F\,P_k\bigl(R_t(\epsilon_{i,F})\Gamma_E\bigr)=1_{R_vE}.$$
Consequently $R_t(\epsilon_{i,F})\Gamma_E\,k_!(\rho_F)$ has open-adjunction transpose $1_{P_kR_tF}$, so equals $\epsilon_{k,R_tF}$. Substitute the formula for $B_0$ from Step 3, use naturality of $\Gamma$ with $\beta$, and use naturality of $\epsilon_k$ with $A$ to obtain (*). These are adjunction naturality and the triangle identity; no tensor, projection or exchange map is cancelled.

source.place: Worker-written explicit open-counit calculation for the proper-reduction mate identity

proof.text:
Write $\delta_o$ for the normalized open tensor map with the extended object in the first slot. Identify $P_kJ\cong N$ by the open unit. Define
$$\nu=k_!(\sigma_{N,P_kL_0})\,\delta_{k;N,L_0}\,\sigma_{L_0,J}:L_0\otimes J\xrightarrow{\sim}k_!(P_kL_0\otimes N),$$
$$\eta=\epsilon_{k,L_0}\otimes1_J:k_!P_kL_0\otimes J\to L_0\otimes J.$$
Then $\eta$ is an isomorphism and
$$\nu\eta=\delta_{k;P_kL_0,J}.\tag{**}$$
Indeed, the open tensor maps identify both source and target of $\eta$ with an object in the fully faithful image of $k_!$. Restriction to $Z$ makes $\eta$, $\nu$, and the displayed $\delta_k$ the identity on $P_kL_0\otimes N$, with the two symmetries in $\nu$ cancelling. Full faithfulness of open extension proves (**) and invertibility of $\eta$. This uses only the normalization and full-faithfulness clauses of the open-tensor lemma.

source.place: Worker-written source-side open tensor comparison in the proper-reduction calculation

proof.text:
The open factor in $\operatorname{PF}_q$ is
$$d=\gamma_{j_q;P_pM,N}:K\otimes P_vN\xrightarrow{\sim}K_D.$$
Define $w=i_!(d)\,\delta_{i;K,P_tJ}:m\otimes P_tJ\to u_!D$. It is related to the displayed $e$ by the explicit equation
$$w=e\,(\chi\otimes1_{P_tJ}).\tag{***}$$
Both maps in (***) have source canonically isomorphic, by $m=u_!P_pM$ and the open tensor comparison, to $u_!D$, and target $u_!D$. Their restrictions to $P$ are $1_D$: $\beta$, $d$, the open tensor comparisons and $e$ have that normalization, while the open counit $\chi$ restricts to the inverse of $\beta$ followed by the open unit identification. Full faithfulness of $u_!$ therefore proves (***). In particular, $w$ itself is not claimed to be $e$; its source is $m\otimes P_tJ$, whereas $e$ starts at $F\otimes P_tJ$.

source.place: Worker-written target-side open normalization, including the missing counit

proof.text:
Set
$$\Psi=\Gamma_{K_D}\,k_!R_v(d)\,k_!(\pi_{v;K,N})\,k_!(B_0\otimes1_N):k_!(P_kL_0\otimes N)\to R_tu_!D.$$
By [def-exchange-projection], these are exactly the exchange $B_0$ and the proper/open factors of $\operatorname{PF}_q$, followed by the triangle mate of Step 2. Let
$$z=R_b(\sigma_{J,L_0})\,\pi_{b;J,L}\,\sigma_{L,R_bJ}:L\otimes R_bJ\to R_b(L_0\otimes J).$$
Expanding $\operatorname{PF}_g$ for $(k,b)$, its open factor is $\delta_{k;N,P_bL}$. The symmetry immediately after $\operatorname{PF}_g$ in $T$ changes this factor to $\nu$. Thus, in the chosen compactification coordinates,
$$T=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b(\Psi\nu)\,z,\qquad
\Omega=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b\bigl(\pi_{t;F,J}(A\otimes1_J)\bigr)\,z.$$
These formulas display both the actual $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,a,b,H}$ and $\pi_b$ contributions. They follow by substitution of the specified definitions; no $q$-exchange or $k''$ open factor is inserted into $\operatorname{PF}_q$.

source.place: Proper reduction: full expansion of the actual $T$ and $\Omega$ factors

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] to $(i,v,k,t)$ with objects $K$ on $W$ and $J$ on $\overline Z$. Both vertical maps are proper and both horizontal maps are open by Step 2. Its identity, followed by $R_ti_!(d)$ and using naturality of $\Gamma$, is
$$\Gamma_{K_D}k_!R_v(d)\,k_!(\pi_{v;K,N})\,\delta_{k;R_vK,J}
=R_t(w)\,\pi_{t;m,J}(\Gamma_K\otimes1_J).$$
Precompose with $k_!(B_0)\otimes1_J$. Naturality of $\delta_k$ in its first input and (**) identify the left side with $\Psi\nu\eta$. Thus
$$\Psi\nu\eta=R_t(w)\,\pi_{t;m,J}(s\otimes1_J).\tag{****}$$
The projection-mate identity is valid on arbitrary unbounded objects, so no finite Tor-amplitude or constructibility assumption enters this application.

source.place: Mate identity in the proper-reduction paragraph, now with the typed source and target maps

proof.text:
Use (***) in (****), naturality of the ordinary projection in its first input $\chi:m\to F$, and (*) to calculate
$$\begin{aligned}
\Psi\nu\eta
&=R_t(e)\,R_t(\chi\otimes1)\,\pi_{t;m,J}(s\otimes1_J)\\
&=R_t(e)\,\pi_{t;F,J}(R_t(\chi)s\otimes1_J)\\
&=R_t(e)\,\pi_{t;F,J}(A\otimes1_J)\eta.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the open-tensor isomorphism $\eta$ of Step 5. Apply $R_b$, precompose with $z$, and postcompose with $\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}$. The two expansions in Step 7 and naturality of $\kappa_{b,t}$ at $e$ give $T=R_c(e)\Omega$. This is ordinary composition and naturality of the defined maps. Neither a projection map, an exchange map nor $\chi$ is inverted.

source.place: Worker-written final diagram chase after the proper/open projection-mate identity

proof.text: Finally compare any original choices defining the forward maps with the displayed choices. The compactification-coherence theorem supplies common refinements and normalized comparisons satisfying the cocycle. The projection-refinement lemma gives the commuting square for each $\operatorname{PF}$ factor, including the base-changed compactification of $q$. Item 4 of [fix-lem-exchanges] gives that square for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ on its witnessed domain. The composition theorem gives independence of $\alpha$ under those comparisons. Symmetry is natural. Pasting these squares shows that $T$ for the original choices equals the $T$ calculated above after the specified source and target identifications. The calculation applies separately to every displayed pair $(aj,bk)$, so it also proves the assertion for any such pair, without asserting refinement naturality of an unspecified product route. Every compared tensor input has the bounded-below etale-origin witness explicitly required in the item.
